title: Light Sources & How Light Travels
source: Science G3 B2 Study sheet pp.4-6, 11; Worksheet Q1-Q2

scenes.t: Light is a type of energy that lets us see the world around us. Light comes from light sources.
Natural light sources are made by nature: the Sun, stars, lightning and fire. The Sun is our main natural light source.
Man-made, or artificial, light sources are made by people: a light bulb, a candle, fireworks and a torch.
We can measure light with a light sensor or a data logger. The unit for measuring light is Lux.
Light travels in a straight line from its source. Shine a torch across a dark room and you can see the straight beam!
Make a hole in the middle of 3 cards and line them up with a torch. You can see the light. Move one card up and the light is blocked!
Light does not bend. When an opaque object is in its path, it blocks the light and makes a dark area behind it. This is a shadow.
The Moon, a mirror and water look bright, but they are NOT light sources. They only reflect light from somewhere else.

activities.title: The Three-Card Test
activities.goal: Prove that light travels in a straight line.
need: play dough to stand the cards up
activities.safe: Never shine the torch into anyone's eyes.

predict.q: If you move one card up, will you still see the light?

steps.t: Ask an adult to make a hole in the middle of each card, in exactly the same place.
Stand the cards in a line using play dough, with the holes lined up.
Shine the torch through the first hole and look through the last hole. You can see the light!
Now move the middle card up a little and look again.

activities.result: When the holes are in a straight line you see the light. When one card moves, the light is blocked.
activities.why: Light travels only in a straight line. It cannot bend around the card.
